title: Ezekiel 22:17–22
context: The LORD’s word comes again to Ezekiel with an image from metalworking: the house of Israel has become dross, the worthless residue of refining, mixed with bronze, tin, iron, and lead (22:18). The LORD will gather them into Jerusalem as into a furnace and melt them in his wrath (22:19–22). In context the image points to the coming judgment on the city. Isaiah 1:22–25 and Jeremiah 6:29–30 use related refining language.

verses.text: The LORD’s word came to me, saying,
verses.arminianNotes: Ezekiel reports, “The LORD’s word came to me, saying,” introducing a new image. Arminian readers see the oracle moving from a list of sins to a picture of refining that explains their judgment.
verses.reformedNotes: Reformed readers likewise see a fresh word beginning. Readers in this tradition note that the furnace image that follows interprets the coming siege of Jerusalem as God’s judgment on a corrupted people.

verses.text: “Son of man, the house of Israel has become dross to me. All of them are bronze, tin, iron, and lead in the middle of the furnace. They are the dross of silver.
verses.arminianNotes: “Son of man, the house of Israel has become dross to me.” Arminian readers see Israel pictured as the worthless residue left when silver is refined, mixed with lesser metals.
verses.reformedNotes: Reformed readers likewise see the image of dross. Isaiah 1:22 and Jeremiah 6:29–30 use similar refining language, cited by reference, and readers in this tradition note the shared image without merging the passages.

verses.text: Therefore the Lord GOD says: ‘Because you have all become dross, therefore, behold, I will gather you into the middle of Jerusalem.
verses.arminianNotes: “Because you have all become dross, therefore, behold, I will gather you into the middle of Jerusalem.” Arminian readers see the city itself becoming the furnace where judgment falls.
verses.reformedNotes: Reformed readers likewise see Jerusalem as the furnace. Readers in this tradition commonly connect the gathering into the city with the siege, while holding precise historical correlations with caution.

verses.text: As they gather silver, bronze, iron, lead, and tin into the middle of the furnace, to blow the fire on it, to melt it, so I will gather you in my anger and in my wrath, and I will lay you there and melt you.
verses.arminianNotes: “As they gather silver, bronze, iron, lead, and tin into the middle of the furnace, to blow the fire on it, to melt it, so I will gather you in my anger.” Arminian readers see judgment pictured as smelting.
verses.reformedNotes: Reformed readers likewise see the furnace image applied to wrath. Readers in this tradition note that, unlike some refining images, this one stresses melting in judgment rather than recovering pure silver.

verses.text: Yes, I will gather you, and blow on you with the fire of my wrath, and you will be melted in the middle of it.
verses.arminianNotes: “Yes, I will gather you, and blow on you with the fire of my wrath, and you will be melted in the middle of it.” Arminian readers see the intensity of judgment pictured in the blowing of the fire.
verses.reformedNotes: Reformed readers likewise see the fire of wrath. Readers in this tradition note the repetition of melting language, which drives home the certainty and severity of what is coming.

verses.text: As silver is melted in the middle of the furnace, so you will be melted in the middle of it; and you will know that I, the LORD, have poured out my wrath on you.’ ”
verses.arminianNotes: “As silver is melted in the middle of the furnace, so you will be melted in the middle of it; and you will know that I, the LORD, have poured out my wrath on you.” Arminian readers see judgment revealing God.
verses.reformedNotes: Reformed readers likewise see the refrain of knowing the LORD. Readers in this tradition note that the image ends not with purified silver but with recognition that the LORD has acted in judgment.
